messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT 1779998887 - smart-routing anomalies detected :warning:  
ops-bot: Elevated fallback rate from policy `smart-routing-v3` -> multiple region hops, error rate rising from 0.6% -> 7.8% in last 3m. Counts: 502s and high tail latencies.

mira: paging @derek oncall — can you take? looks like a routing/fallback loop, might need manual override

derek: on it. ack. joining logs now. pulling recent decisions for smart-routing-v3

derek: quick note — seeing a lot of requests routed to `model-x-quant8` in eu-west-2, but downstream compatibility checks show those tokens cause transformer errors for some callers -> 502. fallback tries next region, then comes back. loop.

tess: confirm. saw similar in traces: request -> eu-west-2 (quant8) -> us-west-2 (fp16) -> fallback to eu-west-2. TTL of fallback set to 30s, so rapid retries.

mira: what's current mitigation? any customer-facing throttles or hold? cs reports latency spikes for some EU customers

csm-lina: getting messages from 3 enterprise customers in EU complaining about degraded chat latency and occasional errors. No data exfiltration reported. high priority.

derek: temp mitigation plan: 1) stop automated cross-region fallback on policy `smart-routing-v3`, 2) force-route traffic for impacted routes to a stable region, 3) scale capacity if needed. Doing step 1 now.

derek: `redwoodctl policy update smart-routing-v3 --set fallback.enabled=false --reason "emergency disable fallback until policy mismatch fixed"`

derek: disabled fallback.enabled, applying change... :hammer_and_wrench:

ops-bot: POLICY UPDATE applied (smart-routing-v3) by derek at 1779998892

tess: confirm change propagated to control plane. good.

derek: next, manual route override to pin routes from eu customers to us-east-1 (lower latency for these customers than bouncing to quantized variant). doing manual override now.

derek: `redwoodctl routing override --selector "route:customer:eu-*" --region us-east-1 --reason "emergency pin to avoid quant8 mismatch" --force`

derek: override submitted, waiting on propagation. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

tess: seeing a new side-effect — the override created a mismatch in model variant mapping. some paths expected `model-x` but now get `model-x-quant8` table entries because region aliasing uses old mapping.

mira: f***, that's the loop we feared. manual override caused control plane to fallback to variant aliases which then triggered retry rules in the runtime.

ben: i'm taking over the oncall at 02:10 UTC — handoff from derek. derek, what's the current state?

derek: handing off. disabled fallback, forced routing to us-east-1, but now observed persistent 502s for a subset of sessions. suspect mapping table mismatch: `region_alias` missing suffix normalization.

derek: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-12T02:09:41Z routing: override apply route=customer:eu-123 target=us-east-1
2026-03-12T02:09:45Z runtime:error incoming model=model-x expected=model-x fp16 got=model-x-quant8 -> 502
2026-03-12T02:09:46Z routing: fallback attempted -> eu-west-2
2026-03-12T02:09:47Z routing: fallback attempted -> us-east-1
```

ben: ok. immediate steps from my side: 1) roll back the manual override while keeping fallback disabled, 2) put a short rate-limit on affected routes, 3) restore a consistent mapping table. I'll coordinate with eng-runtime.

ben: rolling back override: `redwoodctl routing rollback --selector "route:customer:eu-*" --to previous --reason "rollback faulty manual override"`

ops-bot: ROLLBACK initiated by ben at 1779998925

tess: heads up — rollback triggered a brief surge of retries; I'm toggling the per-route token bucket to 5r/s to dampen the loop.

tess: `redwoodctl config set route.bucket.rate --route "customer:eu-*" --rate 5/s`

csm-lina: letting customers know we have mitigations in place and are rolling back the override. Sending staged update now. :email:

mira: eng-runtime, can you confirm the mapping table fix? looks like one of the model onboarding scripts changed alias names for quantized builds and the policy code expects base model name.

leo (eng-runtime): seeing the bug. model aliaser produced `model-x-quant8` entries but policy router normalizes to base name `model-x`. When we enforced override, control plane matched by region and picked the alias unexpectedly. Pushing fix to normalizer and will sync mapping across nodes.

leo: fix is a hotpatch. applying now to control plane configs: `git revert --no-ff cb1a9d3 && ./deploy/control-plane --env prod --sync-mappings`

ben: after rollback and rate-limit, error rate dropped from 7.8% -> 1.2% over 4m. customer complaints still trickling but much improved.

ops-bot: METRIC update 1779998940 - fallback_rate decreased, latency p95 improving

derek: noted for postmortem: manual overrides should be gated by a mapping sanity check. CLI should warn if alias mismatch detected. We need a runbook change: pre-override check = `redwoodctl routing validate --selector ...` to detect alias collisions.

tess: will add a temporary guard to console: block override if mapping checksum mismatch > 0

ben: handoff notes to next oncall (mira): keep fallback disabled for now until mapping synced and rollout patch applied across all regions; keep per-route rate limit at 5r/s for 15m; monitor customer errors and open CS ticket for impacted customers.

mira: ack. creating incident page and assigning postmortem. Logged as INC-2026-0312-routermismatch. I'll include timeline and commands executed.

csm-lina: customers notified with ETA for resolution ~30m, raising priority support for 3 accounts. no SLA breaches flagged yet but close monitoring.

leo: deploy complete, mapping checksum equal across control planes, re-enabling fallback only after an internal canary for 10m.

ben: re-enable fallback in two minutes for a small percentage (1%) of traffic to test: `redwoodctl policy update smart-routing-v3 --set fallback.enabled=true --set fallback.canary=0.01`

ops-bot: CANARY enabled at 1779998972 by ben

mira: monitoring canary. if any jump in 5xx -> immediate disable and rollback to forced routing off.

ops-bot: CANARY metrics after 6m — stable. no spike. canary healthy.

ben: thanks team. moving to mitigated state. I'll file the postmortem with root cause: model alias normalization regression + insufficient pre-override validation. Action items: 1) CLI/Console pre-check, 2) mapping checksum alerting, 3) update runbook for manual override handoffs, 4) add opt-in staging canary for overrides.

mira: good notes. closing incident chat but keeping thread for postmortem artifacts. :white_check_mark:
